meta.title: Birds at the Pond
meta.textType: dialogue: new words from a set

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the nature park with Teacher Kim. Ranger Mark waited at his small office near the pond. The water was flat, and the air was warm. He opened a closet and took out four pairs of binoculars. "The park has a lot of wildlife," he said. "Today we look for birds."

Ranger Mark gave each child an identification card. "A painter from our town made these pictures," he said. "Use the card to find the name of each bird." Mia looked at the card and saw a word that she did not know. "What is a heron?" she asked. "It is a tall bird with long legs, and it stands in the water," said Ranger Mark. "It waits quietly, and then it catches a fish."

"Look at the pond," said May. "I can see a tall gray bird with long legs." "It is a heron," said Lily. She looked at the card and found its picture. Leo found another new word on his card. "What is a kingfisher?" he asked. "It is a small blue bird that catches fish," said Ranger Mark. "It is as fast as the wind."

Leo looked through the binoculars, and he began to sing a pop song. The tall heron lifted its head and flew away over the trees. "Oh no," said Leo. Ranger Mark looked at him in a serious way. "Birds do not like loud sounds," he said. "Nature is quiet, and this is a serious rule for visitors." "I am sorry," said Leo, and he put his hand over his mouth.

After ten quiet minutes, a small blue bird sat on a tree over the water. "A kingfisher!" whispered Mia. Everybody looked through the binoculars and did not make a sound. Then the bird dived into the pond and came up with a small fish. "It is very fast," whispered May. Ranger Mark smiled for the first time that morning. Teacher Kim wrote the time and the weather in her notebook.

On the bus home, Lily opened her notebook. "I will write a post for the blog," she said. "The title is Two New Bird Words." Mia wrote the names heron and kingfisher on the card next to the pictures. Leo put a small paper in his bag with the words, "No pop songs for birds."
text.summary: At the nature park, Ranger Mark gives the Explorers a bird identification card. He explains two new bird words with words that the children know, and a pop song makes a bird fly away.
